__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: The Prometheus that scrapes halite-api. The node row also needs the job that scrapes the nodes themselves, which is usually the same server.

description: halite's control plane: the hub, the API, and the node agents. Point it at the Prometheus that scrapes halite-api; the node row reads the nodes' own scrape job and has its own variables.

panels.description: up for this job. EMPTY rather than 0 when the scrape pool failed to build — an unreadable ca_file or token means Prometheus never registers a target, so there is nothing to be down. An empty stat here means every other panel is showing nothing for a reason that has nothing to do with halite.
panels.title: Scrape

panels.description: Nodes holding an open subscribe stream, including any reached through a relay.
panels.title: Nodes connected

panels.description: Nodes holding an issued certificate. The gap between this and the one to its left is machines that should be talking and are not.
panels.title: Keys accepted

panels.description: Enrollment requests waiting for an operator. On a manual-enrollment estate this should return to zero.
panels.title: Keys pending

panels.description: Times the API could not read the hub's exposition. While this climbs every halite_hub_* panel on this dashboard is empty because the API could not read the hub's half, not because the fleet is idle. Usually a missing metrics.show grant for the API's certificate.
panels.title: Hub scrape failures

panels.description: Nodes a dispatched job has not answered. Non-zero for a moment during any run; non-zero for fifteen minutes is a partial outage.
panels.title: Missing returns

panels.description: Seconds until the enrollment CA expires. Every node's identity is signed by it, so this reaching zero takes the whole estate with it — and it is the one certificate nothing renews on a timer.
panels.title: CA expires in

panels.description: Seconds until the soonest node certificate runs out. Negative once one already has.
panels.title: First node certificate expires in

panels.description: Accepted nodes whose certificate runs out within thirty days. A batch enrolled on one afternoon a year ago expires on one afternoon this year.
panels.title: Expiring within thirty days

panels.description: Accepted nodes whose certificate has run out. Counted apart from the panel to its left, so a fixed problem does not look like a growing one. `keys_accepted` does not fall for these: the record is still there.
panels.title: Already expired

panels.description: Enrollment requests the hub answered. `refused` climbing without `pending` is something asking that has no business asking.
panels.title: Enrollments, by result

panels.description: Subscribe streams opened, and closed by reason. A pair of matching slopes is nodes reconnecting in a loop, which reads as a healthy connected count sampled at the wrong moment.
panels.title: Connects and disconnects

panels.description: What the fleet is being asked to do.
panels.title: Dispatched, by function

panels.description: Returns filed, by whether the node reported success. A rising failure rate is the fleet telling you something; one failure is a package mirror having a bad minute.
panels.title: Returns, by result

panels.description: The 95th percentile from dispatch to return, by function. Which functions are slow, and whether that is new.
panels.title: Job duration

panels.description: Jobs whose time to live passed before every node answered. Steady non-zero means the TTL is shorter than the work.
panels.title: Jobs expired

panels.description: Individual states out of every return. `unchanged_test` is a --test run reporting what it would do, which is not a failure.
panels.title: States applied, by result

panels.description: On a converged estate this is flat between deployments. A step means something changed; a slope hours after a deployment means something is not converging and is being re-applied every run.
panels.title: States that changed something

panels.description: The 95th and 50th percentile of how long a node spent applying a state run, out of its own return. A highstate getting slower shows here before anybody complains.
panels.title: State run duration

panels.description: On the hub this family is orchestration. A node's own compile time is in the node row, which reads the nodes' own scrape job rather than this one.
panels.title: Orchestration compile duration

panels.description: `compile_failed` is one that never ran: the tree would not compile, so nothing was attempted anywhere.
panels.title: Orchestrations, by result

panels.description: Time to compile one node's pillar on the hub. Every node asks on every run, so this is multiplied by the fleet.
panels.title: Compile duration

panels.description: Compilations that failed, so a node got no pillar at all. SPEC 12.7 prefers that to a partial one, which makes any value here worth looking at.
panels.title: Pillar failures

panels.description: The first two segments of the tag, because the whole tag would be a series per job.
panels.title: Events published, by tag

panels.description: Events that did not reach the bus, and reactions the queue could not hold. Nothing should ever be dropped: both are bounded queues whose overflow SPEC 26.2 requires be counted.
panels.title: Dropped, by reason

panels.description: How old an event was when a subscriber was handed it. A subscriber that reconnects from an old offset shows as a spike; one that is steadily behind is not keeping up.
panels.title: Subscriber lag

panels.description: Reaction time by tag, and failures by reason. A reaction that is slow holds the queue that the panel above counts the overflow of.
panels.title: Reactions

panels.description: Beacon events arriving from nodes. The hub sees these as ordinary events, so this is the estate's total without any node reporting a metric of its own.
panels.title: Beacon events, by beacon

panels.description: What a node's bounded beacon queue discarded, read out of the overflow event the node sends. Any value here is a watcher whose readings are being thrown away on the machine.
panels.title: Beacon events dropped, by beacon

panels.description: Tree fetches. `roots` is the local backend; a hub serving git shows that here too.
panels.title: Requests, by backend and code

panels.description: How much tree is going out. A step means a large file entered the tree, which every node then fetches.
panels.title: Bytes served

panels.description: Time for one pass over every git remote. Only present when fileserver_backend names git. A remote getting slower until it times out is what this is for.
panels.title: Git fetch duration

panels.description: Refs that are not served. SPEC 13.3 makes a ref that fails verification one that is not served, which is a control rather than a warning — and a signature failure here means a tree the estate is no longer applying.
panels.title: Git refs refused

panels.description: Logins at the API by backend and outcome. An estate moving off local accounts can see whether anything still uses them.
panels.title: Authentication attempts

panels.description: Every decision the hub made, allowed and denied. A rise in denials is either a role somebody got wrong or somebody trying.
panels.title: Policy decisions

panels.description: Tokens that exist and have not expired or been revoked. An estate whose tokens are never revoked has a store that only grows.
panels.title: Tokens live

panels.description: A login mints one and a logout revokes one. Issued climbing while revoked stays flat is normal — most tokens expire rather than being handed back.
panels.title: Tokens issued and revoked

panels.description: The hub's own HTTP surface. Counted by route rather than by path, so a job identifier or a file name is not a series of its own.
panels.title: Requests, by route and code

panels.description: The 95th percentile per route. `/v1/pillar` and `/v1/files/{path}` are the two every node hits on every run, so they are the ones that make a fleet slow.
panels.title: Request duration, by route

panels.description: The API's own surface, by route and status.
panels.title: Requests, by route and code

panels.description: Two lines: how long the API took to answer, and how long the hub took to answer the API. Where they move together the hub is the slow half; where only the first moves, the API is. Without the second line the only question this could answer was whether it was slow.
panels.title: Where the time goes

panels.description: Requests being answered right now. A wedged service is requests arriving and none finishing: the completed counter goes flat and says nothing about whether that is quiet or stuck. This is how you tell.
panels.title: Requests in flight

panels.description: What the API asked the hub for, and what it got. A zero code is a request that got no answer at all.
panels.title: Requests to the hub, by route and code

panels.description: SSE and WebSocket subscribers holding a stream open.
panels.title: Open event streams

panels.description: Events written to subscribers, and bytes written to every client. A stream that is open and delivering nothing is a filter that matches nothing.
panels.title: Events delivered and bytes out

panels.description: Webhook deliveries received, by path and outcome.
panels.title: Hook deliveries

panels.description: Nodes whose subscribe stream is open, counted on the machines themselves rather than on the hub. A node that thinks it is connected while the hub does not see it is the disagreement worth finding.
panels.title: Agents connected

panels.description: Returns a node discarded because its queue to the hub was full. Any value here is an answer nobody will ever get, and it never reaches the hub by definition — this is the only place it appears.
panels.title: Returns dropped

panels.description: Returns waiting to be posted, across the fleet. Rising is the queue the panel to the left counts the overflow of, before it overflows.
panels.title: Return queue depth

panels.description: Jobs waiting for the executor. SPEC 9.6 runs one at a time behind a bounded queue; a full one is refused and counted as a refusal.
panels.title: Job queue depth

panels.description: SPEC 6.3's structured refusals: a replayed job, an expired one, a malformed one, and `other`, which is mostly a full queue. A refusal is returned rather than dropped, so the hub sees the failure — but not why.
panels.title: Jobs refused, by reason

panels.description: Compiling the tree against applying it. The hub sees one duration per job; these are the two halves, and they get slower for entirely different reasons — a compile that is growing is a tree problem, a run that is growing is a machine problem.
panels.title: Where a state run's time goes

panels.description: SPEC 24's signed bridges. A bridged extension that times out is a job failure with nothing on the hub to say an extension was involved.
panels.title: Extension calls, by result

panels.description: How long a call took, and the ones that ran out of time. A timeout is counted apart from a failure because slow and broken need different answers.
panels.title: Extension duration and timeouts

panels.description: Three different things. A drop is data lost to a full queue; a rate limit is the beacon behaving as configured; a failure is the poll itself erroring.
panels.title: Beacons: dropped, rate limited, failed

panels.description: How long the hub took to answer this node, from the node's side. `/v1/pillar` and `/v1/files/{path}` are what a run waits on.
panels.title: Node to hub, by route

panels.description: What each node started on its own. A schedule entry that stopped firing is flat here and invisible everywhere else.
panels.title: Scheduled jobs, by entry

panels.description: Counted on the machine that ran them, so a node whose returns are being dropped still reports what it did.
panels.title: Jobs run, by result

panels.description: Only present when the hub runs with relay: true. An empty panel on a hub that is not a relay is correct.
panels.title: Subordinate hubs

panels.description: 1 while the relay's link to its upstream hub is open.
panels.title: Upstream connected

panels.description: Returns and events held because the upstream is unreachable. A spool that is not draining while the link is up is the thing to know about before the cap is reached.
panels.title: Spool entries

panels.description: What the spool discarded when it reached its cap. Data the upstream will never see.
panels.title: Spool drops

panels.description: Returns and events the relay passed on. Flat while the spool grows is a link that is up and not moving anything.
panels.title: Forwarded upstream

panels.description: What is deployed, per component. Always 1; the labels are the point. Two rows for one component after a deploy means an old process is still running somewhere.
panels.title: Build identity

list.description: The scrape job name in prometheus.yml for halite-api. `halite` unless you named it something else.
list.label: Job
list.name: job

list.description: Which halite-api to look at, when more than one is scraped.
list.label: Instance
list.name: instance

list.description: The scrape job for the halite nodes themselves — `halite-nodes` in the documented prometheus.yml. Only the node row uses it, and it is empty on an estate where no node sets metrics_listen.
list.label: Node job
list.name: node_job

list.description: Which nodes the node row covers.
list.label: Node
list.name: node_instance
